doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Writing an opera at eight and early exposure to opera
summary: She wrote a little opera, studied a book of opera songs, and could read music and hymns from an early age.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: ... Elements of either restrictions or caveats there. So let’s go back to this, to see if you can talk about this even further. You’re writing early on, you wrote an opera.
A little opera. I thought I wanted it to be an opera. I mean, I didn’t ever get the school performers in the kindergarten to perform it or anything, you know. But it had a
grand opening and finale, lost, I don’t know where it is.
So you never had an opportunity to actually have had it performed.
No. But it was written by an eight year old. Oh, I see, no, Mozart could have done it. Yeah.
Were you exposed to any opera then, cause you say classical music...
Yeah, I was exposed to opera. I had a book of all the opera, Puccini, uhh... who wrote Carmen? Faust? No...
No no no. Duh duh, di di di... uh...
Yeah, I’m drawing a blank on that one. I’ve seen it, I’ve seen my mother sing that.
Yeah, many times probably. [Laughs] So I sang along with it and played the piano.

All the famous songs from all the... this music came from my father, I guess he would pick up something and bring it home to me. And I had hymn books and I knew how to play all the hymns. I could read music from an early age.
And then, so you composed from an early age, at least writing you understood the staffs, of the treble clefs and bass clefs, you understand...
Voices and the ranges, and everything that was part of it.
